item.title: New Operator for Market Arcade Cinemas
item.description: Reels at the Market Arcade cinemas will be spinning again in April. The Buffalo News is reporting that Schenectady-based Scene One Entertainment has signed a five year lease with property owner Benchmark Group for the Theater District complex. Previous operator AMC Theaters let its lease run out at the end of last year. After a refresh of the interior, Scene One is planning to be open April 1. item.title: Call for Short Films: Film Strip Fest Relocates from Atlanta to Buffalo
item.description: Buffalo is now home to Film Strip Fest, which originated in Atlanta, Georgia. This unusual multimedia film festival is a specialized, two-day mini-festival that combines independent short films with live burlesque performances. Film Fest Strip was founded by creative curator and producer Shellie Schmals in 2023. item.description: The D’Youville Kavinoky Theatre continues its mission of presenting “evocative and thought-provoking live theatre” with Hedda Gabler, which runs Feb 27 – Mar 21, 2026. item.title: Locust Street Art Announces Portrait-a-thon: A Live Portrait Drawing Rally
item.description: Locust Street Art has come up with a fun, artistic, and inventive idea for an upcoming fundraiser. Portrait-a-thon: A Live Portrait Drawing Rally involves artists creating live portraiture works of art for event ticket holders. The ticket holders and the artists are matched randomly, upon which time the live painting sessions get underway. item.title: Pegula Backs Heritage Point Project
item.description: After the announcement that the Market Arcade cinemas will be re-opening under new operators in April, downtown received a second bit of good news yesterday. Sabres and Bills owner Terry Pegula has agreed to financially assist the Heritage Point project in Canalside allowing work to restart within weeks.
